about: Hand-labelled pairs of real articles (ids in corpus.json.gz). a, b: the two articles. label: same | different | same-match | related (see scripts/eval-clusters.mjs).

group: how the pair was picked. multilingual: two languages inside one story of the radar. big-cluster: two articles inside one of the 14 biggest stories. same-subject: two stories the language model gave the same subject, kept apart. hebrew-vs-foreign: a story led by a Hebrew article and a foreign one that share a club / player and wording. same-player: two separate stories about one player. transfer: two separate stories about a move / contract of one player. late-source: the first and the last article of a story that kept getting sources for 6+ hours.

by: who decided the label. 'assistant' = Claude read both headlines (foreign ones in the radar's machine translation) and decided; it did not open the articles. editor: null until a Sport5 editor confirms ('confirmed') or corrects the label. No label here has been confirmed by an editor yet: treat the numbers as a careful first reading, not as ground truth.

Pairs were picked by a seeded script from candidates, then every candidate was read; 29 unclear or junk candidates were dropped. The set is a probe of hard cases, not a random sample of the radar: its percentages say how the code does on these cases, not on a normal day.

policy: the label under the clustering rules a Sport5 editor approved on 2026-11-12 (docs/cluster-eval-baseline.md, 'The editorial rules'). same = one story; different = separate stories; review = the headlines are not enough to decide, a person must. The rules were approved by an editor; applying them to each pair was done by the assistant (policyBy), and no pair has been confirmed by an editor (editor is still null). 'label' keeps the first reading and is never overwritten.

relation: same-match = both articles are about one match (they stay related even when they are separate stories); follow-up = one is a later development of the other's affair. phaseA / phaseB: pre_match | live_match | post_match | unknown, for same-match pairs. policyNote: why.
The scores use policy. Pairs with policy "review" are never counted as right or wrong; they are reported on their own.

editorDecision: the decision a Sport5 editor approved on 2026-11-13 (editor-decisions.json): MERGE | SEPARATE_BUT_RELATED | SEPARATE. editor: confirmed (the decision matches the policy label), corrected (it differs), decided (the pair was 'review' and the editor decided it), null (not reviewed by an editor: the labels are the assistant's and unverified). The scores use editorDecision when there is one, else policy. label and policy are never overwritten.
